artists.biography: Metallica is an American heavy metal band. It was formed in Los Angeles in 1981 by vocalist/guitarist James Hetfield and drummer Lars Ulrich, and has been based in San Francisco for most of its career. The band's fast tempos, instrumentals and aggressive musicianship made them one of the founding "big four" bands of thrash metal, alongside Megadeth, Anthrax, and Slayer. Metallica's current lineup comprises founding members and primary songwriters Hetfield and Ulrich, longtime lead guitarist Kirk Hammett, and bassist Robert Trujillo. Former members of the band are bassists Ron McGovney, Cliff Burton, and Jason Newsted, and guitarist Dave Mustaine, who formed Megadeth after being fired from Metallica in 1983.

lastfm.wiki_content: "Reload" is the seventh studio album by the American heavy metal band Metallica, released on November 18, 1997, through Elektra Records in the United States and Vertigo Records internationally. It serves as the follow-up to the band’s 1996 album "Load" and was recorded during the same sessions with producer Bob Rock. Although Metallica initially considered releasing a double album, they decided to divide the material into two separate releases. Additional recording sessions for "Reload" took place in 1997 following the conclusion of the "Load" supporting tour. The album is notable for featuring Metallica’s first guest vocalist, Marianne Faithfull, who appears on "The Memory Remains", and for being the last studio album to include bassist Jason Newsted. Musically, "Reload" continues the hard rock direction introduced on "Load", further distancing the band from its thrash metal origins. The album incorporates influences from blues, country, alternative rock, and grunge, and features instruments uncommon in Metallica’s earlier work, such as the hurdy-gurdy and violin on "Low Man’s Lyric". It also includes "The Unforgiven II", a sequel to the 1991 single "The Unforgiven". Lead vocalist James Hetfield’s lyrics reflect themes of anger, frustration, and personal struggle, drawing inspiration from his difficult childhood. The album’s cover artwork, like that of "Load", was created by artist Andres Serrano using a mixture of blood and urine. Released seventeen months after "Load", "Reload" achieved commercial success, debuting at number one on the Billboard 200 and topping charts in seven countries. Three singles were issued from the album: "The Memory Remains", "The Unforgiven II", and "Fuel". Metallica supported the release with the "Poor Re-Touring Me" tour in 1998. Critical response to "Reload" was mixed; while some reviewers praised the band’s musicianship and stylistic experimentation, others criticised the album for its length and lack of innovation. Retrospective assessments often regard "Reload" and "Load" as complementary works that might have been more effective as a single, condensed release. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
ReLoad (stylized as ReLoad) is the seventh studio album by American heavy metal band Metallica, originally released on November 18, 1997, and serves as the follow-up to their 1996 album Load. Recorded during the same sessions as Load with producer Bob Rock, the album expanded the band's sound to incorporate blues and country influences, featuring guest vocalist Marianne Faithfull on the staple track "The Memory Remains" and utilizing unique instrumentation like the hurdy-gurdy on "Low Man's Lyric." The album is renowned for fan favorites such as "Fuel," "The Unforgiven II," and "The Memory Remains," which have become enduring staples of Metallica's live performances, cementing the record's status as a pivotal work in their hard rock and heavy metal catalog.

The 2026 remaster, released as part of a super deluxe box set via Blackened Recordings on June 26, 2026, offers a comprehensive reimagining of the original classic with the album remastered by Reuben Cohen under the oversight of Greg Fidelman. This massive release includes 15 CDs and four DVDs, containing 301 tracks in total with 245 previously unreleased recordings, including extensive collections of riffs, demos, session takes, rough mixes, and live material from 1997–1998. The box set also features five LPs, a seven-inch single of "The Memory Remains," a 128-page hardcover book with never-before-seen photos, and various memorabilia such as Rorschach Test cards, posters, and tour passes, providing an exhaustive archive for dedicated fans.

Beyond the box set, the remastered edition is available in standard formats, including a 180g double vinyl, a 3-CD expanded edition, and cassette, all featuring the newly remastered audio. The 3-CD Expanded Edition specifically includes the remastered album alongside a selection of Shadowcast rarities and live tracks, accompanied by a 36-page booklet.
